questions.stem: A toddler with tetralogy of Fallot becomes deeply cyanotic and breathes rapidly while crying. What should the nurse do first?

options.text: Place the child in a knee-to-chest position
Lay the child flat on the back
Encourage the child to keep crying
Give a large fluid bolus right away

rationale.correct: Hypercyanotic ('tet') spell: knee-chest, calm the child, oxygen, then morphine and fluids as ordered.

perOption.a: This raises systemic resistance and sends more blood to the lungs.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.stem: For each congenital heart defect, indicate the category it belongs to.

rationale.correct: Classify congenital heart defects by how they change blood flow.

perOption.r1:c1: A left-to-right shunt increases blood flow to the lungs.
perOption.r1:c2: VSD isn't cyanotic in its usual form.
perOption.r2:c2: Pulmonary stenosis with a right-to-left shunt causes cyanosis.
perOption.r2:c3: Its main feature is reduced pulmonary flow.
perOption.r4:c1: A left-to-right shunt increases blood flow to the lungs.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: Which finding suggests coarctation of the aorta in an infant?

options.text: Higher blood pressure in the arms than in the legs, with weak femoral pulses
Equal blood pressure in all four limbs

rationale.correct: Coarctation: compare blood pressures in the arms and legs and check the femoral pulses.

perOption.a: The narrowing limits blood flow to the lower body.

questions.stem: Which findings suggest heart failure in an infant?

options.text: Sweating and tiring during feeds, poor weight gain and tachypnea

rationale.correct: Infant heart failure: feeding problems, diaphoresis, tachypnea, poor growth and hepatomegaly.

perOption.a: Feeding is exercise for infants; heart failure limits it.
perOption.b: Infants with heart failure gain weight poorly.

questions.stem: An infant is prescribed digoxin. The apical pulse is 84/min. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Hold the dose and notify the provider
Recheck in 4 hours and give it then

rationale.correct: Pediatric digoxin: count the apical pulse for 1 full minute and hold per the parameters (infants below about 90 to 110; children below about 70).

perOption.a: Infants usually have digoxin held for a heart rate below about 90 to 110, per parameters.
perOption.b: The heart rate is too low.
perOption.c: The nurse can't adjust the dose.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: A child is being treated for Kawasaki disease with IV immune globulin and aspirin. Which teaching is important?

options.text: Live vaccines such as MMR may need to be postponed for about 11 months after IVIG
Stop aspirin as soon as the fever ends
Kawasaki disease never affects the heart

rationale.correct: Kawasaki disease: fever for 5 days or more, red eyes, strawberry tongue, peeling hands; risk of coronary aneurysm; IVIG and aspirin.

perOption.a: IVIG antibodies can block the response to live vaccines.
perOption.b: Low-dose aspirin often continues for weeks as directed.
perOption.c: Coronary artery aneurysms are the main risk.
perOption.d: Ibuprofen interferes with aspirin's antiplatelet effect.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: A 4-week-old has forceful vomiting after feeds, seems hungry right afterward and has a small olive-shaped mass in the upper abdomen. What does the nurse suspect?

rationale.correct: Pyloric stenosis: projectile vomiting, hunger, olive mass and metabolic alkalosis.

perOption.a: A thickened pylorus causes projectile, non-bilious vomiting and a palpable olive.
perOption.c: Reflux causes spitting up, not projectile vomiting with a mass.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: An 8-month-old has episodes of severe crying with the knees drawn up and red, jelly-like stools. What does the nurse suspect?

rationale.correct: Intussusception: sudden colicky pain, a sausage-shaped mass and currant jelly stools. Report a normal brown stool, which may mean it has reduced.

perOption.a: Telescoping bowel causes colicky pain and currant jelly stools.
perOption.c: This doesn't cause currant jelly stools.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: A newborn hasn't passed meconium in 48 hours and has a distended abdomen. Which condition does this suggest?

rationale.correct: Hirschsprung disease: delayed meconium and later ribbon-like, foul-smelling stools.

perOption.a: Missing nerve cells in the bowel prevent stool from passing.

options.text: Sunken anterior fontanel and fewer wet diapers

rationale.correct: Infant dehydration: sunken fontanel and eyes, dry membranes, fewer wet diapers, tachycardia and lethargy.

perOption.a: These are signs of volume loss.

questions.stem: A toddler with mild dehydration from gastroenteritis is alert and can drink. What should the nurse teach the parents?

options.text: Give small, frequent amounts of oral rehydration solution
Give large amounts of apple juice

rationale.correct: Mild to moderate dehydration: ORS in small frequent amounts, then resume a normal diet.

perOption.a: ORS replaces fluid and electrolytes, and small amounts are tolerated even with vomiting.

rationale.correct: Cleft lip repair: protect the suture line, no prone positioning, elbow restraints and gentle cleaning.

perOption.a: This protects the repair.
perOption.b: Prone positioning risks rubbing the lip.

questions.stem: When should parents collect a tape test for suspected pinworms?

options.text: First thing in the morning, before bathing or using the toilet

rationale.correct: Pinworms: morning tape test, treat the whole family, wash bedding and use good hand hygiene.

perOption.a: Female worms lay eggs around the anus at night.
perOption.b: Eggs are best collected in the morning.
perOption.d: Timing relates to egg-laying, not meals.

rationale.correct: Nephrotic syndrome: proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, edema and hyperlipidemia; treated with corticosteroids.

perOption.a: Massive protein loss causes low albumin and edema.

questions.stem: A child has a suspected Wilms tumor. Which action should the nurse avoid?

rationale.correct: Wilms tumor: post a sign to avoid abdominal palpation and handle the child carefully.

perOption.a: Palpation can rupture the tumor capsule and spread cancer cells.

questions.stem: A parent of a 2-year-old who had a simple febrile seizure asks what to do next time. What should the nurse teach?

options.text: Protect the child from injury, turn the child to the side and time the seizure; call 911 if it lasts more than 5 minutes
Put something in the child's mouth
Put the child in a cold bath
Antipyretics will prevent all future seizures

rationale.correct: Simple febrile seizures are usually benign; teach seizure first aid.

perOption.a: Most febrile seizures are brief and harmless.
perOption.d: Antipyretics are for comfort; they don't prevent febrile seizures.

rationale.correct: Hydrocephalus in infants: increasing head circumference, bulging fontanel, sunset eyes and irritability.

perOption.a: These show CSF building up.

questions.stem: A child with a ventriculoperitoneal shunt has vomiting, headache and irritability. What does the nurse suspect?

options.text: Shunt malfunction with increased intracranial pressure

rationale.correct: Shunt malfunction: signs of increased ICP. Shunt infection: fever and redness along the tract.

perOption.a: Shunt blockage causes CSF to build up.
perOption.b: Shunt failure must be ruled out first.

questions.stem: A newborn has a myelomeningocele. How should the nurse care for the sac before surgery?

options.text: Cover it with a sterile, moist, nonadherent dressing and place the newborn prone
Place the newborn on the back

rationale.correct: Myelomeningocele: sterile moist dressing, prone position and latex precautions.

perOption.a: This protects the sac from drying, rupture and infection.
perOption.b: This lets it dry out and become infected.
perOption.c: This puts pressure on the sac.

perOption.a: Persistent primitive reflexes and abnormal tone suggest CP.

questions.stem: A parent asks whether to give aspirin to a child who has the flu. What is the best response?

options.text: "No, aspirin can cause Reye syndrome in children with viral illnesses; use acetaminophen or ibuprofen instead."
"Yes, aspirin is the best choice for fever."
"Aspirin is safe if given with food."

rationale.correct: Avoid aspirin in children with viral illnesses (influenza, varicella).

perOption.a: Reye syndrome causes liver failure and brain swelling.
